info.desc: Heart Like a Wheel is the fifth solo studio album by American artist Linda Ronstadt, released in November 1974. Featuring Andrew Gold and widely considered as Ronstadt's breakthrough album, it was selected by the US Library of Congress to be inducted into the US National Recording Registry in 2013 for being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically important". The album was placed on the 2020 revised version of Rolling Stone magazine's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time list. .

podcast.body: Released at the end of 1974, "Heart Like A Wheel" was Linda Ronstadt's breakthrough and Grammy Award-winning album. It features a diverse tracklist, including the opening track "You're No Good," background vocals from Sissy Houston on "Dark End of the Street," Maria Moldauer on "Heart Like A Wheel," and a cover of Hank Williams' "I Can't Help It (If I'm Still In Love With You)," with Emmylou Harris. Members of The Eagles (Don Henley, Glen Frey, Timothy B. Schmidt) also played on "You Can Close Your Eyes." While not a "purist country album," it is described as a "purist Linder on Stat album." "Her breakthrough album was Heart Like A Wheel, the Grammy Award winner that was released at the end of 1974."

podcast.body: Released in 1974, this album is described as a moment where the synergy between producer, material, singer, and players created something "otherworldly" in the studio. It features the haunting title track, Linda's arrangement of "Guess I Don't Care Anymore," the Hank Williams classic "I Can't Help It (If I'm Still in Love with You)," and the smash hit "You're No Good." The album charted for 51 weeks and propelled Linda Ronstadt to stardom. "This was heart like a wheel, an album for all time."
